A
continuous glucose monitor (CGM)
is a wearable medical device that tracks interstitial fluid glucose levels 24/7
. It sends real-time data to a smartphone, helping users manage diabetes without frequent fingersticks.
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | CDC (.gov)
Continuous Glucose Monitors vs. Other Wearables
Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM):
Worn on the arm or abdomen, it measures glucose trends and provides high/low alerts.
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | CDC (.gov)
Smartwatch:
Tracks general fitness, heart rate, and steps; some advanced models include optical sensors or basic ECG.
Amazon.in
Wearable ECG:
A dedicated patch or smart accessory that records the heart's electrical rhythm to spot arrhythmias like atrial fibrillation.
National Institutes of Health (NIH) | (.gov)
Sleep Tracker:
Rings, bands, or watches that monitor sleep stages, movement, and heart rate variability.
National Institutes of Health (NIH) | (.gov)
Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM):
A setup where medical devices automatically transmit vital signs (like blood pressure or glucose) to a clinical care team.
National Institutes of Health (NIH) | (.gov)
